newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for April 14.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for April 14.

text.p: Two Gulf of Mexico ports were shut because of storms on Monday, the Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT) said in its 1000 local/1500 GMT daily meteorological report.
Crude ports Pajaritos and Dos Bocas remained closed after storms first shut the ports on Saturday afternoon.
Port officials told Reuters that winds at Pajaritos in Veracruz state were up to 70 km per hour and waves at Dos Bocas in Tabasco state had been up to 12 feet high.

El Mezquital, Frontera, Nautla, Veracruz, Alvarado and Puerto Madero were reported closed to smaller fishing and tourism ships. Smaller vessels were also warned against sailing along the coasts of Tamaulipas, Veracruz, Tabasco, the Yucatan peninsula and the Gulf of Tehuantepec.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Pacific Coast, Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean.

Stronger winds along northern coastline of 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 km/16 to 22 miles per hour) and waves six to eight feet high. Less winds further down coast, except at Oaxaca and Chiapas state coasts.
Cold front losing intensity, leaving rains along coasts of Tamaulipas, Veracruz, Tabasco and the Yucatan peninsula. Winds at 15 to 20 knots with wave heights six to eight feet high.
Partly cloudy with moderate winds from 20 to 30 km per hour.
